calc.winrateDivide: Wins are divided by matches with a recorded result.

calc.poolTotal: The total is every valid match in the period that meets the other filters, whatever champion you play.
calc.definitiveCumulative: It's marked as achieved as soon as you reach the target, even if the period is still open. If you later delete data and drop below it, it goes back to in progress.
calc.definitivePerformance: While the period is open the result is provisional. It's settled when it closes on {end}: with fewer than {minSample} valid matches it's inconclusive.

library.conLosNumerosSon: {value} with {championName}: the numbers are a snapshot, not a verdict. Keep logging; with 10+ matches the analysis gets much more accurate.
library.conTenesUnoDe: With {championName} you have one of your most solid profiles: {numericWr}% WR over {totalGames} matches and a {value} KDA. At this sample size those numbers aren't noise: you're doing something right consistently. The next step isn't playing safer, it's figuring out what you do in lost matches that breaks that pattern.
library.ganasConPeroTu: You win with {championName}, but your KDA ({value}) suggests it isn't through individual dominance. Your value is probably in macro: objectives, map pressure, showing up for key fights. That's hard to see in the numbers, and sometimes it's exactly right. Even so, lowering your average deaths ({deathsAvg} per match) should push your winrate even higher.
library.hayUnaContradiccionInteresante: There's an interesting contradiction with {championName}: your KDA is {value}, but your winrate is {numericWr}%. You're playing well individually, but that edge isn't turning into wins. Ask yourself whether you're closing out games when you're ahead, or prioritizing farm/kills over decisive objectives like Baron or the inhibitor.
library.tuRolConEs: Your role with {championName} is clearly an enabler: {value} average assists against {value2} kills says your impact lives in your teammates' plays. That's not bad, it's a style. The key question is whether that impact holds when your team doesn't turn your plays into kills, because that's where utility champions lose value.
library.conJugasParaKills: With {championName} you play for kills: {value} per match and relatively few assists. That can be a strength if your damage takes out key threats, but it can also mean you're picking solo skirmishes when the team needs something more collective. Check whether your fights line up with map objectives.
library.sosConsistenteConEn: You're consistent with {championName}: in {value}% of your matches you finish with 3 deaths or fewer. The problem isn't survival, it's impact: you don't die, but you don't decide games either. Look to be more aggressive at key moments: take Baron fights, force inhibitors when ahead, call rotations.
library.hayUnaTendenciaClara: There's a clear improvement trend with {championName}: your overall WR is {numericWr}%, but over your last {recentMatchesCount} matches it went up to {value}%. You did something differently, whether in builds, map decisions or matchups you understood better. It's worth figuring out what changed so you don't lose it.
library.tuWrHistoricoCon: Your all-time WR with {championName} is {numericWr}%, but over the last {recentMatchesCount} matches it dropped to {value}%. It could be a meta shift, climbing in MMR or just variance. Before forcing more games, check whether something concrete changed, in the patch, your habits or the matchups you're facing.
library.elDatoMasUrgente: The most urgent stat with {championName} is deaths: {deathsAvg} per match on average is high for any role. Every extra death isn't just a respawn, it's gold given away, a lost objective and ceded map pressure. Cutting down to {value} average deaths would probably have a direct impact on your winrate.
library.estaEnUnBuen: {championName} is in a good spot in the meta (tier score {value}), but your personal winrate ({numericWr}%) doesn't show it. The champion may be strong in the hands of players with a specific style that isn't yours yet. Watch how top ladder players play it: there may be something specific in builds or play patterns you're not applying.
library.estasSacandoDeWr: You're getting {numericWr}% WR with {championName} even though the meta doesn't favor it (tier score {value}). That shows real mastery: you know when it works and when it doesn't. The risk is when the meta hurts it more actively; keep watching whether the results hold up with the patch.
library.inicioPrometedorConEn: Promising start with {championName}: {numericWr}% over {totalGames} matches. It's still too small a sample to be conclusive, but the direction is good. Once you hit 15–20 matches you'll have a much clearer picture of whether it's a pick that helps you or just a good start.
library.tuPerfilConEsta: Your profile with {championName} is balanced: {numericWr}% WR, {value} KDA, {deathsAvg} average deaths. There's no red flag, but no clear dominance either. Your most likely room for improvement is cutting deaths in lost games and forcing more objectives when you're ahead.

legal.about:
Rift Deck was born from a simple idea: help players better understand the game they enjoy.

We believe improving isn't only about reflexes or mechanics. Every match produces valuable information: decisions, patterns, mistakes, wins and learning opportunities. Our goal is to turn that data into useful tools so any player can analyze their performance, optimize their choices and make smarter decisions on the Rift.

The platform brings together stats, builds, match analysis, performance tracking, champion, item and rune information, and strategy tools designed for both casual and competitive players.

Rift Deck is an independent project developed and maintained by {owner}.

## Plans and payments

Rift Deck is currently free and doesn't charge any subscription. If paid plans are offered in the future, their prices and conditions will be published before you can sign up for them, as described in the Terms and conditions.

## Contact

You can write to us at **{email}**.

insights.enTusUltimasPartidas2: In your last {window} matches your winrate was {percent}, versus {percent2} in the previous block. At the same time your average deaths dropped from {value} to {value2} per match. Both changes move together, so your greater stability is a concrete explanation worth validating.
